hints: Focus on what percentage by mass really means, mass of carbon divided by total Mr times 100.
Start with glucose, its carbon mass is $6 \times 12 = 72$ and its Mr is 180, so check its percentage first.
Now work out the same fraction for starch and sucrose and see which ones actually hit exactly 40%.
walkthrough:
**Recall the percentage by mass rule**

Lovely, this is a simple composition calculation. For any compound, the trick is to compare carbon mass to total mass.

$$\% \text{ C} = \frac{\text{mass of C in formula}}{M_r \text{ of compound}} \times 100$$

**Test 1, glucose**

Glucose is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$. Add up the Mr carefully.

$$M_r = (6 \times 12) + (12 \times 1) + (6 \times 16) = 72 + 12 + 96 = 180$$

$$\% \text{ C} = \frac{72}{180} \times 100 = 40\%$$
So statement 1 is correct.

**Test 2, starch and 3, sucrose**

For starch, use one repeat unit $(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_5)$, the n cancels out.

$$M_r = 72 + 10 + 80 = 162$$

$$\% \text{ C} = \frac{72}{162} \times 100 = 44.4\%$$
So statement 2 is wrong.

For sucrose, $\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}$:

$$M_r = (12 \times 12) + 22 + (11 \times 16) = 144 + 22 + 176 = 342$$

$$\% \text{ C} = \frac{144}{342} \times 100 = 42.1\%$$
So statement 3 is wrong.

**Conclude the combination**

Only 1 gives exactly 40% carbon. That matches the combination for 1 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This means 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. While glucose is 40% carbon, starch is about 44.4% and sucrose is about 42.1%, so they cannot all be Q.
options.B: Incorrect. This means 1 and 2 only are correct. Statement 1 is correct but statement 2 is a trap. Students often assume all carbohydrates have the same %C, but starch $(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_5)_n$ has less oxygen and water removed, giving a higher %C of 44.4%.
options.C: Incorrect. This means 2 and 3 only are correct. Both are wrong. Starch gives 72/162 x 100 = 44.4% and sucrose gives 144/342 x 100 = 42.1%, neither is 40%.
options.D: Correct. This means 1 only is correct. Glucose has carbon mass 72 and Mr 180, so 72/180 x 100 = 40% exactly, while the other two have higher carbon percentages.
